subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core session-auth PIN gate, and if so what trusted secret source and verifier path should own it?
rationale: The source shows the enforcement seam exists, but adding a PIN gate would create new core auth config, secret handling, session persistence, and reset semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Sponsor a core security design
options.body: Define the config/secret source, trusted verifier command or internal tool, authenticated SessionEntry state, reset semantics, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Prototype with a plugin first
options.body: Use existing before_tool_call hooks to validate the workflow while leaving core unchanged until the missing semantics are proven.

options.title: Decline the core PIN gate
options.body: Keep the current gateway auth, tool policy, sandbox, and allowlist model and document that per-session PIN auth is outside the current trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core security design
recommendation.body: Define the config/secret source, trusted verifier command or internal tool, authenticated SessionEntry state, reset semantics, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision controls a new auth and secret-handling boundary covered by the repository's security ownership rules.
